notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase on the IT prohibited-use table (A during-work, B general), resolved as during-work because each prohibition is on an act of using a tool; plus incident reporting (when-misuse) and trusted-tool advice. (2) actor on guidance about departments and support offices (A instructor, B admin), resolved by who the sentence names. (3) phase for communication and conferences units in the CTLM principles (course-start vs during-work/when-misuse; during-assessment for conferences). (4) policy type: student work as protected data (P50 over P49), AI code review (P31 over P16), and no identifying information in AI feedback (P50 over P101), each resolved by what the rule protects. (5) unit_stance and modality differences resolved by the sentence's wording (imperative = should; informs only for statements of fact). (6) IT document stance (A delegates, B restrict) resolved as permit: it lists prohibited uses and leaves the rest allowed. Coverage: B added 4 real statements A missed (summarizing, AI praise ideas, colleague conversations, and the 'know and follow' duty), A added items B missed (multilingual benefit, explain-when-AI-hinders, protected-data list items, copyright and provider-terms rationale); 3 A-only units dropped as preamble, repeat, or metadata. Matching treats the two coders' split of the 'Explain/Provide clear instructions' and 'Departments' sentences as aligned pairs.
